metadata.note: Three historical, now-discontinued passenger railroads that served Knoxville, TN, researched from Wikipedia and railroad-history sites in response to a question about whether Knoxville had rail in 1929 -- it did not appear anywhere in this dataset before. The Southern Railway's Bristol-Knoxville-Chattanooga main line (formed from the 1858 East Tennessee & Virginia and East Tennessee & Georgia lines, merged 1869, part of Southern from 1894) carried the Pelican, Tennessean, and Carolina Special. The Louisville & Nashville reached Knoxville from Corbin, KY, giving through service from Louisville. The Louisville-Corbin leg's geometry follows the L&N's actual mainline via Lebanon Junction, Lebanon, Mount Vernon, Livingston, and London, per cincyrails.com's L&N-to-Corbin history and the L&N Lebanon Branch (aka Knoxville Branch, Lebanon Junction to near Mount Vernon) Wikipedia entry -- replacing an earlier straight-line placeholder between Louisville and Corbin. The Tennessee Central Railway's Nashville-Knoxville line (via Harriman, with the final leg over Southern trackage) ran the Volunteer State Limited overnight Pullman service until 1949. All three predate any GTFS/live-data era and have no modern segment (no passenger train serves Knoxville today). Route geometry follows the real intermediate towns each railroad's own history describes, but is a simplified handful of waypoints, not surveyed track centerline. Era boundaries follow real corporate-history milestones (line openings, mergers, discontinuation dates); headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not sourced from real timetables.

metadata.geometry_audit_20260826: The Southern Railway Bristol-Knoxville-Chattanooga main line was re-traced from OpenStreetMap on 2026-08-26, replacing the 4-point straight line described in the note below (which had said the geometry was 'a simplified handful of waypoints, not surveyed track centerline'). It is now 681 points of real track centerline, 245.0 mi, matching the documented ~242 mi. See the feature's geometry_quality for the method, the mileage check and the era caveat. The other two features in this file (L&N Louisville-Corbin-Knoxville, Tennessee Central Nashville-Knoxville) are still coarse waypoint approximations and are NOT covered by this pass.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Sources conflict on when the East Tennessee & Georgia's Cleveland-Chattanooga connector opened: the 1858 segment note in this file says 1858, while southern-railroads.org and the ET&G corporate record give 1859 (29.12 mi, Chattanooga-Cleveland). The 1858 start year has been left as-is pending a check against a primary source. Separately, this feature's segments span three owners (ET&V/ET&G 1858-1869, ETV&G 1869-1894, Southern 1894-1970) in a single feature carrying Southern's colour throughout -- CLAUDE.md Rule 4 would have this split at the ownership-change dates; not done in this geometry pass.

properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap, not approximated: no straight-line legs. Built by shortest-path routing over the ways of OSM route relations 1441353 (NS 'Knoxville District Bristol Line', tagged old_railway_operator=Southern) and 1441354 (NS 'Knoxville District West End'), extended at both ends over the OSM rail graph -- north from the relation's end into Bristol Union Station over the ex-N&W Pulaski District trackage the Southern's trains used to reach the joint station, and west from Ooltewah into Chattanooga over ways tagged old_railway_operator=Southern (NS Chattanooga Terminal District). Two dangling way-ends at the Knoxville junction between the relations were bridged with a 4.15 m connector; every other gap bridged was under 10 m. Douglas-Peucker simplified at 20 m to 681 points, with the point nearest each named station force-kept. Traced 245.0 mi Bristol-Chattanooga against a documented ~242: Bristol-Knoxville traces 132.0 mi against the 130 mi usually cited for the East Tennessee & Virginia; Knoxville-Chattanooga traces 113.0 mi, of which Cleveland-Chattanooga is 30.8 mi against the East Tennessee & Georgia's documented 29.12 mi and Knoxville-Loudon is 29.4 mi. CAVEAT (CLAUDE.md Rule 2): this is the MODERN Norfolk Southern alignment, drawn for all eras back to 1858. The corridor is the original one and the town sequence is unchanged (Johnson City, Greeneville, Morristown, Jefferson City, Knoxville, Lenoir City, Loudon, Sweetwater, Athens, Cleveland), but line relocations since 1858 -- most obviously the 1940s TVA Fort Loudoun and Watts Bar reservoir relocations along the Tennessee River, and terminal rearrangements at Knoxville and Chattanooga -- are not backed out, so the 19th-century segments are drawn on later track in those places. The line was also 5 ft gauge until the 1886 southern-gauge conversion; that changes nothing about where it ran. Endpoints stop where OSM track still exists: 212 m short of Bristol Union Station and 368 m short of Southern's Chattanooga Terminal Station, whose platform tracks are lifted. Replaces a 4-point straight-line placeholder (Bristol - Knoxville - Cleveland - Chattanooga).
